destination.name: Tweed Heads
destination.tagline: The northernmost town in New South Wales, on the Queensland border and the Tweed River mouth.
destination.description: At the mouth of the Tweed River, Tweed Heads is the northernmost town in New South Wales and the twin of Coolangatta across the state line. Cedar cutters were the first Europeans to live in the Tweed Valley, in 1844, and the district later turned to dairying, sugar cane, bananas and fishing. The draws are the Tweed coast headlands and beaches and, about 30 km inland by road, Murwillumbah and the caldera around Wollumbin. The 1994 film Muriel's Wedding used Tweed Heads as the fictional town of Porpoise Spit.
whyVisit: See the Margaret Olley Art Centre

goodToKnow.title: Wollumbin summit closed
goodToKnow.detail: The Wollumbin (Mount Warning) summit track remains closed, and NPWS will decide its future with Aboriginal custodians; the park stays open for the Lyrebird track, picnic areas and camping.

goodToKnow.title: Clocks change at the border
goodToKnow.detail: Queensland does not observe daylight saving, so in summer the time differs by an hour between Tweed Heads and Coolangatta.

goodToKnow.title: Book Tropical Fruit World ahead
goodToKnow.detail: The Duranbah farm opens 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM and closes on Christmas Day; its tractor-train tour costs about 78 dollars, so check the operator's site before driving out.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Autumn and spring, {months}, are mild for rainforest walks and headland lookouts; humpback whales pass the headlands from June to early November.
